subject: Consumption slabs & overage playbook — next steps after demo
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@brightcart.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — consumption slabs, burst expectations, and next steps

Jordan / Priya — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and our asks so we can put a concrete pilot proposal together: 

- BrightCart current expectation: ~50M tokens/month baseline, with up to 7–9M tokens/day during campaigns (you confirmed spikes last week).
- Your budget guidance shared on call: ballpark $700–1,000 / month to start (open to scaling).
- Key decision points for pricing: committed volume (monthly), acceptable $/1M-token target, burst headroom for demos, and overage behavior (rate, notification SLA).

What we’ll deliver next:
1) A short pricing matrix showing committed vs on-demand unit economics and an overage matrix (what we charge beyond quota).
2) Two operational options for handling spikes: a) temporary burst allowance with short grace period and automated throttling after threshold, b) quota auto-increase flow with 48-hour notice for sustained demand.
3) A 3-month pilot proposal with a small committed bucket + burst buffer and runbook for demo-day readiness.

Actions for you: please confirm the 50M/month baseline and whether you need guaranteed latency during spikes (we offer a dedicated pool for prioritized traffic). Also, attach a one-week sample of per-minute usage if you have it (helps set batching/kv-cache profiles).

Attaching a sample CSV template (BrightCart_usage_sample.csv) you can fill. I’ll follow up with a priced pilot doc by Monday.

— Vivek
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@brightcart.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 17:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — consumption slabs, burst expectations, and next steps

Thanks, Vivek — good summary. Confirming the numbers from our side:
- Baseline: ~50M tokens/month (mostly reads, some generation).
- Typical day: 2–3M tokens; peak campaign days: up to 8–9M tokens/day for short windows (2–6 hours).
- Budget: we'd like to keep initial spend < $1,000/month and make sure spike events for marketing demos don’t cause surprise invoices.

Two questions:
1) What does “burst allowance” look like in practice? Do you allow a one-time burst without overage charge and then bill above that? Or do you throttle?
2) If we commit to a small monthly reserved bucket, what’s the unit price we should target to land close to $/1M tokens we discussed on the call?

I attached a small sample export from last week (Priya sent it earlier) — hope that helps.

— Jordan
Director, Product — BrightCart
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@brightcart.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — consumption slabs, burst expectations, and next steps

Jordan — thanks for the sample, that’s perfect. Below is a concise playbook (options + unit economics) so you can take to procurement. I kept calculations simple so you can plug your exact numbers.

Option A — Reserved pilot (recommended for predictable unit economics)
- Committed: 50M tokens / month for 3 months.
- Unit price (committed): $8.00 per 1M tokens.
- Effective monthly cost: 50 * $8 = $400/month.
- Burst buffer: we include a 30% temporary burst allowance (15M tokens) usable for up to 8 hours per month with no immediate overage charge; sustained use beyond that is billed as overage.
- Overage rate: 1.5x committed unit price ($12.00/1M) if usage beyond committed + burst in the same month.
- Auto-raise path: sustained usage >125% of committed for 7 consecutive days triggers an automated quota review with a 48-hour option to accept a temporary increase (pro-rated commit).

Option B — On-demand hosted (no commitment)
- Unit price (on-demand): $12.00 per 1M tokens.
- No burst buffer; we permit short (<=2 hour) spikes up to 200% of recent 24h average at no throttling; anything beyond is billed at 1.6x on-demand ($19.20/1M) and subject to short-term rate limiting to protect latency for other tenants.

Examples (to make the math tangible):
- If you run 50M tokens in a month under Option A: $400/month. If one campaign pushes you to 65M (committed + 30% burst), still $400 for the month. If you hit 80M, the extra 15M billed at $12.00 => +$180 => $580 total.
- Under Option B, the same 80M in a month: 80*$12 = $960 (no discount for commit).

Pilot recommendation: start with Option A for 3 months (committed 50M) to lock unit economics and give you a 15M burst buffer for demos. If you prefer minimal commitment, start On-demand and we can add a short-term burst add-on the week of your campaign.

Operational notes:
- Alerts: we’ll send usage alerts at 60%, 85%, and 100% of committed; overage notification within 1 business hour.
- SLA for temporary quota increases: 48 hours for automated increases, 24 hours for manual escalations (premium).

I’ll attach the pricing estimate PDF and a short pilot SOW. If this aligns, Marissa will follow up with the contracting and billing cadence.

— Vivek
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
